title: Maldives Opposition Eyes Sweeping Constitutional Overhaul
author: Mimrah Abdul Ghafoor
text:
Former Maldivian President and current Chairman of the Maldivian Democratic Party (MDP) Mohamed Nasheed addresses the MDP’s fifth National Congress in Male, Maldives, on Oct. 1, 2026.
Credit: Facebook/Maldivian Democratic Party
The Maldives’ main opposition party, the Maldivian Democratic Party (MDP), held its fifth National Congress from October 1 to 3.The congress, which is the party’s highest decision-making body, adopted significant changes to the MDP’s internal structure. It abolished the posts of party president and vice president, consolidating leadership under the chairperson, a position currently held by former President Mohamed Nasheed. Yet its most consequential decision was the overwhelming endorsement, by 520 of the 563 delegates present, of a sweeping constitutional reform program titled Bodu Badhalu (meaning “Big Change” in Dhivehi).[...]
